newsitem.title: UK: Dollar seen ailing vs yen, even if rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen ailing vs yen, even if rates rise.

text.p: The dollar emerged bloodied and bruised after plunging to five-month lows below 112 yen on Tuesday and analysts say there is little comfort in store - not even from higher U.S. rates.

"The trend is very strongly pro-yen at the moment. And I suspect the dollar will come under pressure even if the Fed raises interest rates this evening," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International.

The dollar skidded to troughs of 111.98 yen to stand down near four yen from 115.93 yen in late Europe after reports Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Partly (LDP) committee was mulling the possibility of requesting higher discount rates from the Bank of Japan in order to rationalise government-affiliated financial institutions.
By 1245 GMT, however, it had bounced from the lows and stood above 113 yen after Japanese officials warned the yen's rise had been too rapid and a rate rise was not likely in the short-term.
The U.S. unit remains anaemic, however, after having lost near 11 percent from 4 1/2 year peaks of 127.46 yen on May 1.

With all eyes now on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later, when a decision on rates will be taken, the dollar could be fooled into thinking that higher rates would boost it against the yen.
But economists, split over the likelihood of a rise in U.S. rates, say even a hike is unlikely to do much for the dollar against the Japanese unit.

"We would not be surprised to see a hike of 25 basis points...But given the momentum of the strengthening yen, it would be surprising to see a reversal. I think we could see a stabilisation," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.
